activity_context.topic_title: Using Integration by Parts to Calculate Integrals With Logarithms

feedback.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{5}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ {v}^{′}=25{x}^{4}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(5x)\cdot (5{x}^{5})-\int \frac{5{x}^{5}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot {x}^{5}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{5}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.$
